Which of the following does the model predict?\x3C/p>",rationale:"\x3Cp>Choice D is correct. The function \x3Cspan>N\x3C/span> is exponential, so it follows that \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"N of d \">\x3C/span> changes by a fixed percentage for each increase in \x3Cspan>d\x3C/span> by 1. Since \x3Cspan>d\x3C/span> is measured in hundreds of meters, it also follows that the number of brachiopod species changes by a fixed percentage for each increase in ocean depth by 100 meters. Since the base of the exponent in the model is 0.90, which is less than 1, the number of brachiopod species decreases as the ocean depth increases. Specifically, the number of brachiopod species at a depth of \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"d plus 100 \">\x3C/span> meters is 90% of the number of brachiopod species at a depth of \x3Cspan>d\x3C/span> meters. This means that for each increase in ocean depth by 100 meters, the number of brachiopod species decreases by 10%.\x3C/p>\x3Cp>Choices A and C are incorrect. These describe situations where the number of brachiopod species are decreasing linearly rather than exponentially. Choice B is incorrect and results from interpreting the decrease in the number of brachiopod species as 10% for every 1-meter increase in ocean depth rather than for every 100-meter increase in ocean depth.\x3C/p>\x3Cp>&nbsp;\x3C/p>\x3Cp>\x3C/p>"},answers:$R[4]=[$R[5]={id:11626,question:3554747798,correct:!1,content:"\x3Cp class=\"choice_paragraph \">For every increase in depth by 1 meter, the number of brachiopod species decreases by 115.\x3C/p>\n"},$R[6]={id:11627,question:3554747798,correct:!1,content:"\x3Cp class=\"choice_paragraph \">For every increase in depth by 1 meter, the number of brachiopod species decreases by 10%.\x3C/p>\n"},$R[7]={id:11628,question:3554747798,correct:!1,content:"\x3Cp class=\"choice_paragraph \">For every increase in depth by 100 meters, the number of brachiopod species decreases by 115.\x3C/p>\n"},$R[8]={id:11629,question:3554747798,correct:!0,content:"\x3Cp class=\"choice_paragraph \">For every increase in depth by 100 meters, the number of brachiopod species decreases by 10%.\x3C/p>\n"}],userData:void 0})($R["server-fn:0"]))
